football_evidence.question: Can Nevada take away New Mexico’s big plays?
football_evidence.assessment: Some measured evidence supports EdgeDesk’s lean toward Nevada, and its own breakdown accounts for about 1.1 of the 2.9 points, but not the full gap. It is a research question, not a bet.
supporting: When New Mexico has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): New Mexico’s offense has allowed a sack on 12.6% of its dropbacks, and Nevada’s defense sacks the quarterback on 8.0% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).
When New Mexico has the ball (third down): New Mexico’s offense converts 38.1% of its third downs, and Nevada’s defense allows opponents to convert 26.8% of their third downs (FBS average 39.6%).
In his last two games (Hawai'i and North Dakota State), Fa'avae averaged 6.0 yards per attempt, against 10.1 in his five games before that.
In his last two games (Oklahoma and UTEP), Moga averaged 4.2 yards per attempt, against 7.3 in his two games before that.
contradicting: When Nevada has the ball (big plays on the ground): Nevada’s offense turns 5.9% of its runs into explosive gains, and New Mexico’s defense gives up explosive gains on 2.7% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.5%).

When Nevada has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): Nevada’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 19.3% of its runs, and New Mexico’s defense stops 29.9% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.5%).

When New Mexico has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): New Mexico’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 14.7% of its runs, and Nevada’s defense stops 12.9% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.5%).

When Nevada has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Nevada’s offense has allowed a sack on 4.4% of its dropbacks, and New Mexico’s defense sacks the quarterback on 9.0% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).
quarterbacks: Carter Jones has completed 53 of 89 passes (59.6%) for 654 yards, 7.3 yards per attempt, 4 touchdowns and 2 interceptions in four games for Nevada, and has been sacked on 7 of 96 dropbacks.
AJ Bianco has completed 31 of 58 passes (53.4%) for 335 yards, 5.8 yards per attempt, 2 touchdowns and 3 interceptions in four games for Nevada, and has been sacked on 0 of 58 dropbacks.
Toa Fa'avae has completed 49 of 88 passes (55.7%) for 790 yards, 9.0 yards per attempt, 5 touchdowns and 4 interceptions in seven games for New Mexico, and has been sacked on 15 of 103 dropbacks.
Luke Moga has completed 23 of 39 passes (59.0%) for 248 yards, 6.4 yards per attempt, 3 touchdowns and no interceptions in four games for New Mexico, and has been sacked on 2 of 41 dropbacks.
